Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s

- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The ants move at constant speeds (3 cm/s for A, 1 cm/s for B, 2 cm/s for C) and reverse direction whenever two meet.  
Simulating the collisions in chronological order gives:

* **First collision** – Ants A and B meet after \(t_1=7.5\) s at position \(\frac{65}{2}\) cm. Both bounce, so now A moves left (speed 3) and B moves right (speed 1).
* From this point onward:
  * Ant A reaches the left end after another \(\Delta t_A=\frac{65}{6}\) s, i.e. at \(t_2=\frac{55}{3}\) s.
  * At exactly the same moment (\(t_2\)), ants B and C meet interior to the rod (at \(\frac{130}{3}\) cm) and bounce: now B moves left (speed 1) and C moves right (speed 2).

After \(t_2\) only two ants remain, moving away from each other toward opposite ends.  
* Ant B reaches the left end after an additional \(\frac{130}{3}\) s → total time \(\displaystyle t_{\text{exit},B}= \frac{55}{3}+\frac{130}{3}= \frac{185}{3}\) s.  
* Ant C reaches the right end after an additional \(\frac{85}{3}\) s → total time \(\displaystyle t_{\text{exit},C}= \frac{55}{3}+\frac{85}{3}= \frac{140}{3}\) s.

The last ant is B, which falls off after  

\[
t_{\text{last}}=\frac{185}{3}\text{ seconds}.
\]

ANSWER: 185/3
